If the property is null (i.e., not set), it immediately throws a FactoryException with a message indicating that no implementation was given for the current factory class. The rest of the method attempts to load the class, find a matching constructor, and create an instance; any failure there also results in a FactoryException with the underlying exception chained. The consistent pattern of throwing FactoryException for all failures indicates an expectation that the caller or an external error-handling mechanism will catch and respond to these exceptions.
